angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 358,286 km at 44.99 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.2257 +/- 0.0138 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 44.99 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.515 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Cherubim et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1695 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..167C/abstract): 358,286 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.513 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Cherubim et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1695 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..167C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3690 +/- 50 K from Cherubim et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1695 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..167C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cherubim et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1695 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..167C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1695.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.725, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
